title: Daily SGS Top 5
tagline: Five stories, one question: who's in control?

stories.headline: The UN aid agency for Palestinians may be shut down
stories.summary: UNRWA's acting head reportedly plans to cut 7,000 to 8,000 of its 15,000 staff, citing a $70 to $100 million shortfall. The plan is not publicly confirmed.
stories.label: Slightly Sovereign
stories.why: A global UN body hands its work to local and regional hands.
stories.what_it_means: Schools and clinics would pass to the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank and the US-backed Board of Peace in Gaza.
stories.economic_impact: Thousands of paychecks at risk where jobs are scarce; some donors warn they may stop paying.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a charity out of money handing its soup kitchen to the town.

stories.headline: Australia's interest rate hits an 18-year high
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its rate to 4.85%, its fifth hike of 2026 and the highest since 2008. The board split 6 to 3.
stories.label: Neutral
stories.why: A national bank doing its normal job.
stories.what_it_means: Australia is fighting high prices on its own terms; inflation is not expected back in its 2 to 3% target until late 2027.
stories.economic_impact: A $500,000 home loan costs about $77 more a month.
stories.everyday_example: It's like turning down the heat in a too-warm house while everyone grabs a sweater.

stories.headline: Venezuela's new foreign minister visits Washington
stories.summary: Oliver Blanco met Rubio and Bessent on Nov 2, the first top-level meeting since Maduro's capture in January.
stories.label: Moderately Sovereign
stories.why: Venezuela pulls away from Russia, China and Iran toward its own elections.
stories.what_it_means: The US backs a three-step plan: stabilize, recover, then free elections.
stories.economic_impact: Washington wants more Venezuelan oil pumped and its banks reconnected to the world.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a neighbor helping fix your house so you can run it yourself again.

stories.headline: Belgium's prime minister offers to quit over the budget
stories.summary: Bart De Wever offered his resignation after his five-party government failed to agree €10 billion in cuts and taxes for 2027. The King holds it until Friday.
stories.label: Slightly Globalist
stories.why: EU deficit rules set the deadline and the size of the cuts.
stories.what_it_means: The fight is over who pays: top earners or spending cuts.
stories.economic_impact: The deficit was 5.2% of GDP in 2025 and rising; no deal risks pricier borrowing.
stories.everyday_example: It's like roommates who can't split the rent while the landlord says pay in full.

stories.headline: Iran opens the door to talks, and oil plunges
stories.summary: President Pezeshkian says the Supreme Leader gave his government powers for peace talks with the US. Brent fell 7.6% to $104.77, the biggest one-day drop since July.
stories.label: Neutral
stories.why: Two nations bargaining, no global body in charge.
stories.what_it_means: Iran may bargain, but wants sanctions lifted and the blockade ended before reopening Hormuz. Nothing is agreed.
stories.economic_impact: Cheaper oil could ease fuel prices worldwide.
stories.everyday_example: It's like the guy blocking the road saying he'll talk, and prices drop before the car moves.
